display_name: Early-warning and command sources an Osa battery can listen to besides its PU-12
status: Library of source TYPES (simcore/c2_sources.hpp, roadmap E4 / 7.8). A scenario's "c2" block makes instances of them (a place, a net, outages). The PU-12M itself is data/command/pu12.json and always the main source. Every number cited; most timings are labelled estimates because no operator document gives them. See docs/research/EM_C2_SOURCES_2026-10.md for what is known about each.
notes: Cadence (update_period_s) is how often the source tells the vehicle a new picture; designation_range_m is how close to the BATTERY a target must be before it is read out to the vehicle; max_range_m is how far from the SOURCE it can see (for a radar source the radar horizon applies as well). plot_error_* is a fresh error on every plot (measurement noise); navigation_error_* is the fixed error of the source's own survey and orientation, drawn once.

sources.display_name: Early-warning radar site on a voice net (P-19 / P-18 / P-12 class)
sources.notes: A regiment's or division's early-warning radar site reads aircraft out over VHF voice: azimuth, range, height. The Osa regiment's own control battery had a P-19 (Soviet) or P-40, two P-19 and a P-18 (NVA) beside the PU-12M; a P-19 could also be attached to a battery (exercises). flak11 and korovin_tiv_2010 give the equipment; no document gives the voice timings.

antenna_height_m.source: estimate (a truck- or trailer-mounted metric/UHF early-warning radar antenna stands a few metres up)

link_range_m.source: estimate (VHF line of sight, limited by the vehicle's R-123M antenna: the Polish manual gives the R-123M 12 km with the vehicle's radars on, 15 km off, mon_2112_80, via data/em/osa_ak.json; a high-power set with a mast reaches further). With the EM layer on this is replaced by the radio link budget.

update_period_s.source: estimate (an EWR turns every 5-10 s, but each target is read out by voice, 12 s each: the net can carry one fresh picture of a few targets about every half minute)

max_range_m.source: samsim_osa p20 (the plotting board's outer ring); nato_radar_refs (P-19 instrumented range 260 km); fm100_2_3 p. 5-138 (Flat Face 250 km, NATO belief)

radar_battery_number.source: estimate (a tactical number for the EWR battery; samsim_osa p20 shows 62 for the PU-12's radar battery)

navigation_error_deg.source: estimate (a surveyed site oriented to north to within a fraction of a degree)

plot_error_deg.source: estimate (a metric/UHF early-warning radar's azimuth accuracy read off the scope by a plotter is of the order of a degree; ew_textbooks class value)

plot_error_m.source: estimate (range read off a scope with a 1-2 km resolution cell)

designation_range_m.source: samsim_osa p21 (the crew waits until the target approaches the 50 km range circle); applied to this net by estimate

operator_delay_s.source: estimate (the same as the R-123M's operator delay in data/em/osa_ak.json)

message_s.source: estimate (one target read out: number, azimuth, range; the same as the R-123M's message time in data/em/osa_ak.json)

pass_on_s.source: estimate (the vehicle commander passing the designation to his crew)

sources.display_name: Division early-warning radio net (broadcast of preliminary target data)
sources.notes: Soviet motorised-rifle regiments' short-range air defence (the SA-9) had no radar of its own and relied on preliminary target data broadcast over the division early-warning radio net until the crew saw the target (fm100_2_3, SA-9 'limitations', PDF p. 322, the US Army's 1991 account of what it believed). An Osa battery attached to a division can hear the same broadcast. Coarse, slow, one broadcast for every listener.

link_range_m.source: estimate (a divisional early-warning net is a VHF broadcast over a division's width; a hand-held reception range of tens of kilometres)

update_period_s.source: estimate (a coarse broadcast: one picture a minute, like the PU-12 board's hand plotting, samsim_osa p20)

max_range_m.source: estimate (the picture of a division's radar-technical unit reaches well beyond the front)

radar_battery_number.source: estimate (a tactical number for the division's radar unit)

navigation_error_deg.source: estimate (broadcast data are coarse: a few degrees)

navigation_error_m.source: estimate (coarse broadcast data; flak11 gives the PU-12M navigation error as 5 degrees and 3 km, and this net is worse than a dedicated post, not better)

designation_range_m.source: samsim_osa p21; applied to this net by estimate

operator_delay_s.source: estimate (a net control station reads a broadcast call: slower than a post addressing one vehicle)

message_s.source: estimate (a broadcast read out slowly enough for many stations to copy)

sources.display_name: Neighbouring Osa battery's radar picture by radio
sources.notes: Batteries exchange what their own radars see, so a jammed or blind vehicle can be fed by a neighbour or by the regiment (video_osa, tier 4, consistent with flak11). The neighbour is another Osa vehicle: its range is the Osa search radar's, not an early-warning radar's.

antenna_height_m.source: estimate, from the search radar definition in data/em/osa_ak.json (calibrated at 5 m)

link_range_m.source: mon_2112_80 (the R-123M reaches at least 12 km with the vehicle's radars on, 15 km off), as recorded in data/em/osa_ak.json

update_period_s.source: estimate (the neighbour's operator reads out his picture when a new target shows: about every 20 s, faster than the PU-12's plot)

navigation_error_deg.source: estimate (the neighbour's heading reference, set by the same drills as ours)

plot_error_deg.source: estimate (an Osa search radar read by an operator)

designation_range_m.source: samsim_osa p21; applied by estimate (the neighbour's own range is the limit)

sources.display_name: Visual air-observation post (field radio or telephone)
sources.notes: Armies the system served kept visual air-observation and reporting units: Serbia's VOJ branch dates to 1915 and its 126th brigade passed on the air situation through the 1999 campaign (voj_serbia, tier 4 press). Soviet-model VNOS posts did the same. Nothing here is from an operator document: every number is an estimate, and the existence of the practice is the point.

link_range_m.source: estimate (a field telephone line or a short-range VHF set to a post a few kilometres out)

update_period_s.source: estimate (an observer calls aircraft as he sees them)

max_range_m.source: estimate (a fighter-size aircraft is made out by eye at a few kilometres in good visibility)

radar_battery_number.source: estimate (a tactical number for an observation post)

navigation_error_deg.source: estimate (an observer with a compass or map)

plot_error_deg.source: estimate (a bearing by eye or binoculars)

designation_range_m.source: estimate (only close targets matter to a post this near)

message_s.source: estimate (a short call: direction, type, height guess)

sources.display_name: Digital data link from a higher command post (PU-12M7 / PPRU-1 era)
sources.notes: The later PU-12M7 takes one analogue radar and three digital sources (AWACS, radars and automated command systems), holds 99 targets and links by radio to about 40 km and by wire to about 15 km (pu12m7_page, tier 4). The PPRU-1 'Ovod' reconnaissance and command post can run up to three batteries (ppru1_refs, tier 4). The Czechoslovak army planned PU-12 battery posts able to receive from the air force's automated system (vr_1994_pvov). Included so a later-era or what-if scenario can use it; a 1980s Osa-AK scenario should not.

link_range_m.source: pu12m7_page (radio data link up to 40 km)

update_period_s.source: estimate (a digital track list refreshed every radar scan or two)

max_range_m.source: pu12m7_page (the PU-12M7 display reaches 100 km range, 25 000 m altitude)

navigation_error_deg.source: estimate (a digital link carries the source radar's own accuracy)

operator_delay_s.source: estimate (no operator: a track is sent as data)

pass_on_s.source: estimate (the vehicle commander sees it on his display)
